([BK08, Definition 1.4]).

A Frobenius-constant quantization of a Poisson variety $X$ over a field $k$ characteristic $p>0$ is a quantization $A$ of $\mathcal{O}(X)$ and an algebra map

(3.18)

$\Lambda:\mathcal{O}(X)^{(1)}\to Z(A)$

such that $\Lambda(f)\equiv f^{p}$ mod $\hbar^{p-1}$ .

The map $\Lambda$ in the data of a Frobenius-constant quantization is also called a Frobenius splitting, as it splits the surjection $A/k\hbar\to\mathcal{O}(X)$ on the subalgebra $\mathcal{O}(X)^{p}$ of $p$ -th powers of functions on $X$ , which is identified with $\mathcal{O}(X)^{(1)}$ .

Now we fix a conical Hamiltonian symplectic resolution $X\to Y$ , its universal deformation $\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}$ and the canonical quantization $\mathcal{A}$ of $\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{X})$ . We assume that this quantization is equipped with the structure of a Frobenius-constant quantization, that is there exists a Frobenius splitting

(3.19)

$\Lambda:\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{X})^{(1)}_{\lambda}\to Z(\mathcal{A}_{p\lambda})$

where $\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{X})_{\lambda}$ denotes the $T$ -weight $\lambda$ functions on the universal deformation and $\mathcal{A}_{p\lambda}$ is the $T$ -weight $p\cdot\lambda$ part of the quantization. Such maps indeed exist for:

•

Springer resolutions: classically the Frobenius center of asymptotic universal enveloping algebra (crystalline differential operators) gives the desired splitting [BK04, Proposition 3.5] [BMR08, Section 1.2],

•

Coulomb branches for a gauge theory associated with $(G,V)$ (for abelian $G$ , these recover hypertoric varieties), by the construction of [Lon21].

We use the map $\Lambda$ to define multiplication operators acting on the $D$ -module of twisted traces as follows. Fix $\bar{x}\in\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{X})_{0}$ , an element of the universal coordinate ring of torus weight $0$ .
card.label: Definition 3.13

paper.title: 3D mirror symmetry in positive characteristic
paper.abstract: Via the formulation of (quantum) Hikita conjecture with coefficients in a characteristic $p$ field, we explain an arithmetic aspect of the theory of 3D mirror symmetry. Namely, we propose that the action of Steenrod-type operations and Frobenius-constant quantizations intertwine under the (quantum) Hikita isomorphism for 3D mirror pairs, and verify this for the Springer resolutions and hypertoric varieties.
